title: U.S. House · Alabama's 2nd Congressional District
area: South-central and southeast Alabama, including Montgomery and stretching to the Georgia and Florida state lines.

context.text: Incumbent Shomari Figures (D), elected in 2024 to what was then a newly redrawn, more competitive district, advanced without a primary. A new congressional map signed into law in 2026, after the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling, moved this district's primary to August 11, 2026 (the primary originally scheduled for May 19 was voided). Alabama state Representative Rhett Marques won the August 11 Republican primary. Cook Political Report rated the district R+7 for 2026.

candidates.name: Shomari Figures
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District (since 2025)

summary.text: Shomari Figures is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District, elected in 2024. A Mobile native and University of Alabama law graduate, he worked in the Obama White House and Department of Justice, for Sen. Sherrod Brown, and as deputy chief of staff and counselor to Attorney General Merrick Garland under President Biden. He sits on the House Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and is seeking a second term.

background.text: Raised in Mobile, Alabama, and educated there from kindergarten through law school, according to his congressional biography; his father, Michael Figures, was a state senator and lawyer, and his mother, Vivian Figures, served on the Mobile City Council and is a state senator.
Graduated from John L. LeFlore High School in Mobile; earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and history (2006) and a J.D. (2010), both from the University of Alabama.
Clerked for a judge on the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri and worked on President Obama's re-election campaign.

In the Obama administration, served in the White House as Domestic Director of Presidential Personnel and then as White House Liaison at the Department of Justice, according to his congressional website.
Worked in the office of U.S. Senator Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio); his congressional website also lists service as Counsel in Congress.
Worked on the Biden-Harris transition team, then returned to the Department of Justice as deputy chief of staff and counselor to Attorney General Merrick Garland.
Won the April 16, 2024 Democratic primary runoff over Anthony Daniels (61.1%) and the November 2024 general election over Republican Caroleene Dobson (54.6% to 45.4%) in the redrawn 2nd District.
Assigned to the House Agriculture Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee for 2025-2026.
Advanced from the 2026 Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot; married to Dr. Kalisha Dessources Figures, with four children, according to his congressional website.

priorities.text: Access to healthcare, citing Alabama's non-expansion of Medicaid and high rates of maternal mortality, particularly for Black mothers and infants.
Investing in education, citing low reading and math proficiency rates in Alabama and low teacher pay.
Jobs and economic opportunity, including raising wages, supporting small businesses, expanding childcare access, and workforce development.
Combating gun violence, citing Alabama's high rate of gun deaths, while saying any approach should protect residents' constitutional rights.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he will build on the Affordable Care Act and expand healthcare networks and community health centers; he also cosponsored H.R. 3069, the Medicare for All Act.
Campaign website says he will work to protect reproductive rights and ensure patients can make their own healthcare decisions.

Cosponsored H.R. 3115, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, a bill "to regulate assault weapons"; his campaign website also describes a "holistic approach" to gun violence while pledging to protect residents' constitutional rights.
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025, a bill to provide for increases in the federal minimum wage.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture subcommittees) and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management; Highways and Transit; Water Resources and Environment subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Rhett Marques
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 50.3% of the vote over five other candidates.
candidates.currentRole: Member, Alabama House of Representatives, District 91 (since 2018)

summary.text: Rhett Marques is a Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives (District 91) since 2018 and a small-business owner, and the Republican nominee for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District. He won the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary with 50.3% of the vote, and he serves as Vice Chair of the state House Commerce and Small Business Committee.

background.text: Born and raised in Spanish Fort, Alabama; graduated from Fairhope High School in 1990 and earned a marketing degree from the University of Alabama in 1994.
Served as owner and manager of Goodson Tire & Auto before entering the legislature.
Elected to the Alabama House of Representatives, District 91, in November 2018 after winning the Republican primary runoff over Lister Reeves Jr.; re-elected in 2022 and took office November 7, 2018.

Has served on the Commerce and Small Business Committee (Vice Chair since 2023) and the Health Committee since 2019; his 2025-2026 assignments also include Transportation, Utilities and Infrastructure.
Is not running for re-election to the state House in 2026; described by 1819 News as a representative from Enterprise.

Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary in Alabama's 1st District; those primary results were later voided, and new primaries were held August 11 after federal courts allowed the state to use previously barred congressional maps.

Won the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary for the 2nd District with 50.3% (15,468 votes), ahead of Hampton Harris (20.4%); 1819 News reported endorsements from President Trump and U.S. Sen. Katie Britt.

priorities.text: Says making life more affordable for Alabama families will be his top priority in Congress, including eliminating wasteful federal spending and lowering taxes.
Says he will work to cut regulations on businesses and support onshoring supply chains and domestic manufacturing.
Says he will fight to keep border and immigration enforcement policies in place, citing support for "Detain and Deport" over "Catch and Release."

positions.summary: Campaign website says he will fight to keep criminal immigrants out of communities and continue "Detain and Deport" policies rather than "Catch and Release."
Campaign website says the right to protect oneself is "God-given" and guaranteed by the Second Amendment, and that he will not let the Left take it away.
Campaign website (quoted on Ballotpedia) says he is pro-life and will work to defund Planned Parenthood and bar taxpayer money for ending life.

record.text: Has served in the Alabama House of Representatives, District 91, since 2018; currently Vice Chair of the Commerce and Small Business Committee and a member of the Health and Transportation, Utilities and Infrastructure committees (2025-2026 term).

candidates.researchNotes: Marques' Ballotpedia page lists a campaign website statement that appears to describe an Alabama 1st District campaign; the issue statements cited here are drawn from that same statement, which addresses statewide/national themes not specific to a district.
